lines: Every product artist knows this folder.
Final. Final, really.
And no one remembers which one the client approved.
What if every look lived in one file?
Takes for Blender.
Stage management for product visualization.
Takes runs the stage behind every shot.
The camera, the world, the materials, the animation, and the render settings.
It starts with one tree.
Scene groups, scenes, view layer groups, view layers, and takes.
With a live preview beside every shot.
Then, the cascade.
Set a camera, a world, or a preset on any level, and everything below inherits it.
Until a deeper level says otherwise.
And every preset slot resolves on its own.
Every take is one round of review.
Write down the client's note, click New Take from Here, and work it in.
Earlier rounds stay one click away.
Variant Switch shows one product in every finish.
Build the parts once, and save each look as a state.
Every shot picks its own, and nothing is ever duplicated.
Each view layer wears its own animation.
Switch shots, and every object picks up the right action.
Anything you haven't keyed goes home to its rest pose.
Pin the exceptions, like a logo that spins the same in every shot.
Parent State passes animation down the cascade, all the way to the lowest take.
Each take can add its own keys on top, so simple actions combine into complex motion.
It works for materials too. Set a look once, and every child take follows.
Diff State colours the viewport by where each value comes from.
This take, a parent tier, the rest pose, or drift.
Modes change how the file behaves.
Still Mode pins stills to frame zero.
Value Lock snaps accidental nudges back.
And every active mode shows as a pill in the viewport.
Multi-Cam cuts one take between several cameras.
And every take keeps its own edit.
Tags label anything, in colour.
Rules bundle a whole render setup, and apply it on any tier in one click.
In the sequencer, every strip plays with the take it will render.
The preview is the edit.
Then, deliver.
Batch render every shot and every variant, in the foreground, or in the background while you keep working.
Estimate times up front, resume where you stopped, and retry only what failed.
Smart Output names every file from tokens, even your own.
So each render lands in the right folder.
Work fast, with six pie menus,
bookmarks for any animatable property,
and tool settings that stay in sync across every scene.
Open files made without Takes, and keep the animation, cameras and worlds they had.
Project presets travel with the file, so everyone who opens it gets the same setup.
An AI assistant can drive Takes too, every change a single undo step.
Takes for Blender.
One file. Every look. Every render.
